prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web application comp, 16:10 landscape
Primary request: create a second compositional option for "Inference Track", a personal eight-week production LLM inference roadmap tracker for a Java backend engineer.
Surface structure: no marketing hero and no conventional sidebar. Use a two-register benchmark ledger composition. A narrow upper register spans the page and shows overall completion as eight precisely numbered week cells, with the active cell "03" expanded slightly. The large lower register is a single working sheet for the active week, organized on strict ruled columns: left column goal and hours, center column checklist of concrete deliverables, right column proof-of-work and notes. At the bottom edge, show a quiet preview line for the next week. The screen should make current work and accumulated evidence visible at once.
Content: active week is "03 · Benchmarking & tuning". Deliverables are "Run an open-loop load test", "Record TTFT, TPOT, queue time", and "Publish the benchmark report". Include labels "PROOF OF WORK", "HOURS · 6 / 16", and "NEXT · 04 QUANTIZATION". The eight stages are Foundations, Java gateway, Benchmarking, Quantization, Observability, Kubernetes, Reliability, Capstone.
Visual world: contemporary inference benchmark result sheet and engineering run log, not vintage. Off-white matte ground, near-black ink, deep green status ink, pale sage rules. Tabular numerals, crisp alignment, square check controls, minimal rounded corners, no floating cards.
Focal moment: the active-week working sheet is large and calm; completed week cells above retain small proof counts.
Typography: practical workhorse sans with a compact technical face for week numbers and metrics.
Constraints: shippable real product UI, not poster art; accessible contrast; no gradients; no glassmorphism; no illustration; no photography; no decorative icons; no sidebar; no charts beyond a restrained linear progress indicator; no fabricated benchmark values; no watermark.
